why: Timestamps never decrease, so for each ad the clicks inside the last k minutes form a time-based sliding window. A per-ad deque keeps the clicks in order; at COUNT time pop old ones off the front and report the length.
hints: Because time only moves forward, a click that is too old for one query is too old for every later query.
Keep a hash map from ad id to a deque of click timestamps. New clicks go on the back.
On COUNT, pop from the front while the timestamp < t - 60*kMinutes + 1, then answer len(deque). Each click is pushed and popped once: O(total operations).
pitfalls: The window is inclusive: a click at exactly t - 60*kMinutes + 1 still counts.
A COUNT for an ad never clicked returns 0.
Operations with the same timestamp are processed in input order, so a click just before a COUNT at the same second is included.
